text:
maria: quick follow-up from the RFC thread — we still need to pick where region/cost/latency penalties live. runtime vs sidecar tradeoffs only. keep replies short so we can decide by EOD

devon: +1. my hot take: runtime = single-hop, lowest added p95, but ties us to runtime release cadence. sidecar = flexible rules and safer rollout but adds RPC on hot path.

kevin: telemetry cost is real. if we evaluate heavy scoring per request in sidecar we blow token budget for high qps tenants. do we have numbers?

anya: i ran a quick sim yesterday. baseline runtime eval (inline) adds ~0.8ms p50 and ~1.6ms p95 on our L4 models at 100k rps. sidecar (RPC) adds ~3-4ms p50 and ~6-9ms p95 depending on network hop.

luis: thanks @anya. so runtime seems better for tight-latency tiers. what about maintainability? sidecar wins there for iterating policies without full deploys.

maria: agree. also consider config explosion: runtime needs compact policy DSL, sidecar can accept richer DSL but then more compatibility surface.

devon: one hybrid option: keep a minimal critical evaluator in runtime (region affinity, tier caps, hard denies) and forward complex scoring to a policy service async or as shadow checks. that gives fast-fail decisions inline and richer scoring for observability/rollouts.

kevin: hybrid sounds promising. but we must specify the contract: what keys are available inline vs remote, and how to handle divergence. suggestion: runtime exposes a small typed policy API, e.g.

```
// runtime policy contract (pseudocode)
policy_input: { tenant_id, model, seq_len, region_hint }
policy_output: { hard_allow: bool, hard_deny: bool, soft_penalty: float }
```

anya: +1 to typed surface. soft_penalty could be a normalized 0..1 multiplier we apply to cost weight. also include a version field so runtime can reject unknown shapes.

luis: rollout plan idea: start with shadow mode where sidecar returns soft penalties and runtime logs divergence. then enable canary where runtime reads sidecar suggestions for a <1% traffic slice. finally flip to runtime for hard checks for latency tiers.

maria: action items then: (1) devon to draft minimal runtime policy contract (by tomorrow) (2) anya to produce microbench numbers for hybrid (p95/p50/qps) (3) kevin + luis to design rollout playbook and failure modes (circuit breaker, fallback to default).

devon: will do. draft will include schema, expected compute cost, and a compatibility/versioning story.

ops-bot: canary-checklist created: https://x/repo/canary-policy-rollout.md (assigned: kevin, luis) :white_check_mark:

kevin: quick question — if sidecar unavailable, runtime should default to permissive or conservative? my vote: permissive for availability, but add strong telemetry and alerts.

anya: i prefer conservative for security-heavy tenants, permissive for public ones. maybe make it tenant-configurable with global default permissive.

maria: tenant override + global default sounds right. add to action items: product to define per-tenant safe default.

luis: i will add extreme-failure tests to chaos suite (simulate sidecar lag/drop and ensure fallback path).

maria: ok. last note — keep policy DSL examples small so we can compile easily into runtime bytecode, e.g.:

```
if region != client_region then penalty += 0.2
if model in expensive_models then penalty += cost_weight * 0.5
```

maria: thanks all. if no objections i'll mark hybrid approach as tentative decision and start RFC follow-up with concrete API and rollout steps. :thumbsup:

kevin: :+1: no objections.

anya: :thumbsup: final question for later — how do we surface explainability in logs for customer support? will add to follow-up.

maria: noted. will add to RFC follow-up doc.
